summary: Steel lookout tower, 30 m (98 ft), with a 2014 construction year in Alberta's lookout dataset; listed active. No source describes public visits.

staffing.status: listed active; Alberta says its lookout sites are each staffed by an observer, generally April to October

facts.agency: Alberta Wildfire, with Agriculture and Forestry

events.note: Alberta's lookout dataset gives 2014 as the year constructed; the listed type is steel

evidence.supports: steel entered boreal tower construction in the 1920s and gradually displaced wood
evidence.quote: Introduced in the 1920s, steel increasingly replaced wood for tower construction.

evidence.supports: boreal forest context for the tower types
evidence.quote: In the boreal forest area, a variety of tower types evolved
127 wildfire lookout sites are located throughout Alberta's boreal forest

evidence.supports: each site staffed by a lookout observer, generally April to October
evidence.quote: Each site is staffed by a lookout observer whose job is to watch for wildfire all day, each day, generally from April to October.

evidence.supports: wildfire staff with Agriculture and Forestry have adopted BearSmart recommendations for many sites
evidence.quote: Wildfire staff with Agriculture and Forestry have adopted a number of Alberta BearSmart recommendations for many of their sites

evidence.supports: campground open seasonally May to October

sources.title: Wildfire Lookouts of Alberta (FIReS layer query)

notes_for_editor: 1) Year, type, height and active flag come from one provincial dataset that its own metadata marks Protected (not for general-public maps). The story uses only those four values, no coordinates or access codes; an editor should confirm that citing the layer is acceptable. 2) No source read describes public access to this site, so the brief's 'closed' is neither confirmed nor corrected, and no access fact is recorded. 3) The staffing and BearSmart sentences are Alberta's general descriptions of all 127 lookout sites, not site-specific records. 4) No history before 2014 was found. 5) The MD of Opportunity campground page names the lake's campground but says nothing about the lookout, so the story keeps the two apart and no local unit is named for the lookout. 6) Search budget: 3 websearch.py queries, because the first two returned no lookout-specific pages.
